h1: AI UGC Video Ads Guide: Creator-Style Clips for Your Shop
lead: UGC here means a clip that looks like a creator filmed it. Make one from a product photo or a product link, with a script (the words to say), a person on screen, and a voice. That person is not a real customer.
secondary_keywords: short video ads for small brands
summary: UGC means a creator-style ad from one photo or a product link, with the words, a voice, and a person on screen. The person is not a customer.

sections.h2: What is an AI UGC video ad?
paras: It is a short ad made from your product, a short sentence you type, or a product link. The file includes a script, a person on screen, a voice, and the edited clip, with no film crew and no separate editor.

Tall is 9:16 and fills a phone. Square is 1:1 for a scrolling post. Wide is 16:9. You can also use 4:3 or 3:4. Publish it on [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok), [Instagram](page:plat-instagram), or [Facebook](page:plat-facebook). The person is made by the tool, so the clip is not a customer's review.

sections.h2: See what a creator-style ad looks like
paras: Pick the shape before you spend credits. Credits pay for each clip. A tall clip fills a phone. A square file sits in a scrolling post. A wide file fits a screen.
The pictures on this page use one jar so you can see the hand, the lid, and the room. Your file should do the same: the product is already doing something in the first moment.

sections.h2: How to make a video ad with AI in 3 steps
paras: Paste a product link or upload one photo, and name the action you want on screen.
The tool writes the script, picks a person on screen and a voice, and edits the clip.
Download the shape you need and publish the file on TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram.

Remember: the person is made by the tool. Do not give them a buyer's name. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. You see that cost before you start. Paste the product link in [URL to video](page:url-to-video), or pick the person in the [actor library](page:ai-actors).

sections.h2: What should the clip start with?
paras: The video should start with the product already doing something. Do not start on an empty room or on a person with empty hands.

For a jar, open the lid, scoop a little product onto a hand, or hold the jar up to a mirror. One action per clip. A 10-second video has room for that moment and a little of the room, not a whole story.
sections.alt: Hands pull plain gray skincare jar from a tote onto a bathroom counter.

sections.h2: How long should the ad be?
paras: Use 6 or 10 seconds for one action, 15 when the product has to be used, and 30 for a fuller showing. Pick 9:16 so the clip fills the phone.

Six seconds is a lid coming off and costs 24 credits. Ten seconds fits that action plus a second look and costs 40. Fifteen can take the product out, use it, and set it down, and costs 60. Thirty leaves room for a longer showing and costs 120. You see the number before you start.

Use 1:1 for a square scrolling post, 16:9 for a wide screen, and 3:4 or 4:3 when the place you post asks for that shape. Each length or shape is a new clip. For a clip of the product in use, start with the [AI product video generator](page:product-videos).

paras: The file includes the spoken line, captions, and music you are allowed to run in an ad. Read the captions before you publish, and fix a wrong word before the ad is posted.

Keep the words off the bottom and the right edge of a tall video, where the app buttons sit. The upper middle of the picture is a safer spot. Do not ask for famous faces or logos you do not own. Those may be refused. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded.

sections.h2: Can I present the person as someone who bought it?
paras: No. Do not give them a name, a made-up history, or a quote that says they bought it and reviewed it.
Talk about what the product is and how it is used. Make another version when you want a different room or a different first action.
One photo or a product link, a script, a person on screen, a voice, and a length of 6 to 30 seconds.
The person is made by the tool. Say what the product does, not that a customer said so. A finished clip can be used in ads, and it has no watermark. There is no free plan.

faq.q: What is an AI UGC video ads tool?
faq.a: A tool that makes a short ad from a product, a sentence you type, or a product link. You get the script, the person on screen, the voice, and the edited clip. This page is the shop guide for that job. The person is not a real customer.

faq.q: How do I create the ad?
faq.a: Paste a product link or upload one photo. Let the tool write the script and match a person on screen and a voice. Then download the shape you need and publish it on TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram.
Shops that need many ad versions from the products they already sell, in the shapes paid ads use. It is for many short ads, not one single film.
No. There is no free plan and no free first clip. Plans start at $24.50 a month for 200 credits. A download has no watermark.

faq.q: Can I use the clip in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. A finished clip can be used in ads, and it has no watermark. Add nothing that says the person is a customer.

faq.q: Which shapes and platforms can I use?
faq.a: Tall (9:16), square (1:1), wide (16:9), plus 4:3 and 3:4. That covers [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok), [Instagram](page:plat-instagram), [Facebook](page:plat-facebook), and [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts).

faq.q: Can I make ads for many products?
faq.a: Yes. You can run a batch, a group of clips, across the products you choose. Each clip shows its credit cost before it starts. A 10-second clip is 40 credits. Six seconds is 24, fifteen is 60, and thirty is 120. If a job fails, those credits come back.
Shops use them to try more opening lines. A creator can still film your main product. This page does not promise a sales result.

faq.q: Will TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram reject the ad?
faq.a: Do not say the person is a customer. Ad rules change, so read the current TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram rules before you spend. The [Content Policy](/content) is ours. Their ad rules are theirs.

faq.q: What if the clip shows a part my product does not have?
faq.a: Do not post it. Make the clip again and name the exact action and the exact product in the sentence.
